title: Considerations for a Credibility Assessment Framework in Model-Informed Drug Development: White Paper

content.abstract_summary: Adapts the ASME V&V 40 risk-informed credibility framework to Model-Informed Drug Development (MIDD). Defines how model risk (model influence × decision consequence) dictates the necessary level of verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification required for regulatory decision-making.
key_findings: Establishes a standardized credibility assessment framework for MIDD based on the ASME V&V 40 standard
Model risk is formalized as the product of Model Influence (how heavily the regulatory decision relies on the model) and Decision Consequence (severity of consequences if the model is wrong)
Defines specific V&V activities: code verification, calculation verification, model applicability evaluation, and sensitivity/uncertainty analysis
Serves as the direct conceptual foundation for the FDA 2025 AI/ML 7-step credibility framework and ICH M15 guidance
limitations: Written prior to widespread integration of deep neural ODEs and hybrid ML models in MIDD submissions

extracted_claims.text: Model credibility is context-dependent and should be commensurate with the model risk, which is determined by the decision consequence and model influence.

gaps_addressed: Provides the primary peer-reviewed citation bridging ASME V&V 40 to MIDD and pharmacometrics for regulatory workstreams and White Paper Section E

provenance.notes: Added 2026-08-29 by Antigravity review. Core regulatory bridge paper translating ASME V&V 40 into pharmacometric MIDD credibility assessment.
